beats.name: Hook
beats.vo: Power goes out at 2 a.m. Does your homelab shut down cleanly, or does it just crash?

beats.name: Hero
beats.vo: This is homelab-nut: Network UPS Tools, set up from your laptop.

beats.name: The old way
beats.vo: Normally, a graceful shutdown across machines means configs, SSH keys, scripts, systemd units and alerts. It's a multi-day project.

beats.name: Two commands
beats.vo: homelab-nut turns all of that into two commands.

beats.name: Step 1: init
beats.vo: Step one: init. Guided forms describe your fleet: which box has the UPS, which are clients, and what needs a clean power-off.

beats.name: Step 2: plan + apply
beats.vo: Step two: plan shows every change before it happens. Then apply configures every host over SSH.

beats.name: The outage
beats.vo: Now when the power drops, a battery-watch daemon counts down and shuts everything off in order: desktop, NAS, and the gateway last.

beats.name: Sleep through it
beats.vo: And you sleep right through it.

beats.name: Outro
beats.vo: It's open source. The docs are at docs.torcato.dev/homelab-nut, and if it saves your rack, give it a star on GitHub.
